title: Regions, availability zones and their effect on latency

videos.script: Before you create anything in a cloud account, you pick a region. {{menu}} It looks like a setting in a menu. It is the most physical decision in this course. A region is a place on a map, with buildings, power lines and fibre. Your data lives there. Your prices are set there. And your users are a certain distance away from it. {{map}} Distance is time. Light in glass covers about two hundred kilometres in a millisecond, and nothing on the internet goes faster. From São Paulo, a server in Virginia is at least seventy-six milliseconds away, there and back. You will compute that number yourself, and see what it does to a page that asks twenty questions in a row. {{light}} Inside a region there are zones. They are separate buildings with their own power, kilometres apart. They exist so that one fire does not take your application down with it. Using two of them costs money, and you will see exactly how much. {{zones}} Then the bigger failures. A whole region in trouble, and what it costs to keep a second one ready. And the edge, which sits close to your users and is not a region at all. {{edge}} By the end, you should be able to choose a region and defend the choice with numbers. {{end}}
